x: Harry after a not very good day, finished 27th with evergreen Bob Readman 42nd, Bill True 49th, Syd Spencer 63rd and Cyril Yescombe 66th. Since this event Cyril has shown considerable improvement and looks like being an asset to the team next year.
Len Demmon trailed the Captain home in 3.13.13 with Bob Readman and Bill True just behind, followed by Cyril Yescombe continuing to show improvement.

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

Norman was well up for the Kilos with Bob walking well under control and Harry doing the same. Len Demmon, off night work and Cyril Yescombe were further back. Pace began to tell and positions changed.

There was a total of 46 walkers from this country including six of our members, viz; George Place, Cyril Yescombe and Syd Spencer in the Police team and Ber[illegible]ard Eglington, Jack Goswell and myself in the R.W.A. team, with Sid James and Ron Kim as attendants.

George Checkley 7th and Hugh McGreechan 9th, looked pretty good packing, but unfortunately our fourth man, Cyril Yescombe, who is quite a newcomer to distance racing, although making a brave effort, could do no better than 27th, which lost us 2nd team place by one point.
Hugh McGreechan won the Police Barking to Southend Race for the fourth time. Cyril Yescombe was 10th and won the handicap. Eric Hall won the Civil Service 2 miles Championship.

Bob Readman, Sid Spencer, Gerry Plaice and Cyril Yescombe were noticed having a steady training spin, probably discussing the advantages or disadvantages of Constabulary duties and civilian life, and Bernard Stevenson had a few behind him this time.

A trio of Hugh McGreechan, Bob Newson and Norman Guilmant were at this time some three minutes behind with George Beecham, Harry Shields and Cyril Yescombe completing the team a further 2 minutes back.
Cyril Yescombe was perhaps a trifle disrespectful to our President by showing him the way home but we were very happy to have our eight men in 47 scoring positions.
The President came next in 3.10.47 and he was followed by Fred Rolfe, ever improving Cyril Yescombe on his first 20. George Beecham was obliged to retire with leg trouble.
George Beecham was 7th after overcoming a bad spell in 3.47.37 and Cyril Yescombe who was very strong over the second half, clocked his best time for the distance in 4.55.44.
Fred Rolfe finished 24th, Cyril Yescombe 39th and Bert Stallard 49th out of 82 finishers. Times of our walkers who were the only club to finish a full team of eight were:

Of our others, Cyril Yescombe and Harry Shields had their usual social outing, and George Place and Syd Spencer seemed to enjoy their trip round this corner of Middlesex which still has fields and trees to show something remaining of a rural atmosphere.
Our team was completed by Cyril Yescombe, and thereafter the Belgrave vests followed in at intervals until we had finished twelve men of the 107 completing the course.
Bernard Eglington, back from service in Germany was always ready to step into the breach if needed and Cyril Yescombe maintained his progress.

Support, if necessary, was always at hand, for Cyril Yescombe scored 8th (actual 11th) and earns our hearty congratulations on gaining his Honours Badge; our sympathies to Bernard Eglington on missing his by one place.

Halfway times were not outstanding; Eric and Terry Clark were still leading with Ray Hall in 3rd place closely followed by Cyril Yescombe and George Beecham who were about three minutes in front of George Checkley.

Cyril Yescombe was very short of training but was having a go for several reasons. Percy Wilson was this year representing the Wilson clan and the other Bel. was Fred Rolfe who unfortunately had to give it best at Crawley.

With George Williams being passed by Clark(Poly) at 5 miles, when lying in 3rd place, and Ray Middleton walking home in 12th position, we had the low team score of 18 points. 1st M.P.A.A. member on handicap without award: C.Yescombe 61:29(12:5)
Our Cyril Yescombe won the handicap. We now look forward to the longer distances and shall do our utmost to regain the 20 miles and 50 kilometres Championships which were taken last year by Met.
Fotheringham was maintaining a short lead over Cyril Yescombe and Johnny Morris, and a little further back still, Bert East had his eyes set on catching George Checkley and another handicap award!

The Belgrave 'A' team seemed to have the race nicely sewn up when, at 3 miles, one of the team was ruled out (he shall be nameless!) Thus Cyril Yescombe, for what must be the first time, was called on to complete what still proved to be a winning 7 miles team.
Cyril Yescombe was first Belgravian home, in 5th position, with G.
The 'A' team finished 10th, with Ray Middleton 6th (97.04), Ken Bailey 32nd (109-13), Cyril Yescombe 33rd (109-27), and George Bates 44th (111.24); 111 finished.
Gerry Cameron produced a surprise packet when in only his second 10 mile race he came through to finish our third man home, 32nd in 88:27 with Cyril Yescombe not far away in 38th position.

George Checkley showed that he is returning to his old form after a 2 year layoff, Cyril Yescombe improved on his seasons best times by over 2 minutes, but Dave King after travelling up from Bournemouth was unfortunately pulled early in the race.

- George Checkley finished 11th in the Middlesex "20" and his form (final time 3:10.23) suggests that he is slowly returning to fitness. In the same race Cyril Yescombe was timed at 3:36,47 in finishing 24th.
First Belgravian home was Cyril Yescombe (90:55) in 19th place, well ahead of MacLennan (96:48) 38th, J. Wilson (98:22) 45th and Fotheringham (98:54) 47th.

Another keeping his eyes open for potential talent is Cyril Yescombe, who is the Met. Police Northern Area liason officer to the Police Cadets.
We mourn the passing of Cyril Yescombe, aged 47, and our sincere condolences are extended to Mrs Yescombe, who has helped us so often, and her family.
The tragic loss of Cyril Yescombe is a blow to us all. It is men like Cyril that carry a club through it's lean years, and his sense of humour and loyalty to Belgrave will be sadly missed.

The next "B and B" (1963) saw two Belgravians doing the journey stride by stride, Cyril Yescombe (another Police stalwart) who died tragically a few years ago and Bernard Eglington, former runner from Derby and R.A.F. man.

By walking step for step with the late Cyril Yescombe from Brighton to London and back he became Centurion No. 344. Now living in the Colwyn Bay area he keeps himself fit and we are always glad when he makes a trip to town to line up with the Bels team.
Bonnie Yescombe, and she asked after many Club members. Many will recall her late husband Cyril's purposeful walking for Club and Police teams.
